_comment: What we have actually run, not what we recommend. Models age in weeks and this file is
fetched at runtime for that reason: a name compiled into the installer would still be
advertised long after it stopped being a sensible choice, and the installer does not
update itself.
Rules for adding a line here:
- only models someone on the project has actually run the instruction suite against
- 'note' says what was observed, in one sentence, with no superlative
- observations, never a verdict: the suite is a heuristic on free text and the machine
matters as much as the model. So nothing in this file ranks anything - no field says
which is best, and the order of the entries carries no meaning. A program showing them
IS free to put the most useful first so somebody knows where to start; that is its
decision to make and defend, not something this file settles. The person testing decides.
- NEVER pick or rank by language. Sorting by 'good at Japanese' would break the rule the
whole project is built on: every part of it stays language-agnostic.
WHAT IS WORTH MEASURING, which this file used to leave unsaid. It said what to measure and how
to word it, never what deserved the run — so the shortlist kept filling with whatever happened
to be installed: previous generations, agent models, a family's second-to-last version.
- the LATEST of its family, judged at its WEIGHT and not by its number. A 27B-only release
does not supersede the 9B of the generation before it; nothing else covers that size.
- a weight that adds something to the spread already covered. Two entries a few hundred
megabytes apart, one of them worse on every figure, help nobody choose.
- it must not reason before answering. Every line then costs the thinking as well, in a game,
while somebody waits for text to be replaced.
⚠ A missing language claim is NOT a reason to skip a model. The reference below announces none
and was measured anyway; 'languages' records what a publisher says, and silence is not a claim
that it cannot. Our suite measures, its page does not.
WHERE FROM: the official library. Every entry here comes from one, and a third-party upload is
a decision to defend rather than an addition that passes — the same reasoning the Manager
applies to loader downloads. What a model writes goes into a game's interface, and travels to
everybody else if that translation is published. Weights can carry instructions nobody can see:
a Modelfile's SYSTEM prompt is readable with 'ollama show --modelfile' and should be read, but
a poisoned weight is not detectable by any inspection. Re-uploads add a party without adding
anything else; prefer the publisher over a mirror.
NOTHING IS WITHHELD FOR SCORING BADLY. Every model here can be downloaded, with its figures
and what it missed written next to it. Offering only the spotless ones sounded prudent until
the measurements arrived: it left the smallest cards with no choice at all, on the grounds
that we knew better than the person who owns the machine.
MEASURED THE WAY A GAME BEHAVES, not one request at a time. The mod checks the markers
itself, asks again up to three times when they are wrong, repairs a trailing line break, and
if the model still fails it leaves the line in its original language rather than caching a
mangled one. Every figure below comes from that whole chain — which is why several models
score better here than a single call would suggest: their mistakes get corrected in play.
'typical_s' and 'worst_s' are the wait before the original text is replaced on screen, end
to end. 'retried' is lines that cost two or three requests instead of one — time and graphics
card spent twice over while the game runs. 'refused' is lines left untranslated.
⚠ MEASURED ON ONE MACHINE, ONE CARD, ONE PAIR OF LANGUAGES — see the three fields above.
What a model HOLDS travels: it is a fact about the model. Whether it FITS does not: on a
smaller card the same model is split with the processor, and lines take seconds instead of
tenths of a second. Compare 'vram_gb' against your own card, and let the tester answer for
your machine — it says which of the two happened.
⚠ Language matters too: a model can hold the markers in one language and lose them in
another. The tester runs in the reader's own, which is the real answer.
⚠ Models are unloaded between measurements. Without that, the second model tested inherits a
card the first is still holding and gets split with the processor — one model here read 8.2s
a line that way, and 0.7s once measured on its own. That was our test order, not the model.
'pull' IS PINNED TO A VERSION, NEVER 'latest'. A moving tag makes every figure below a lie
the day it moves, and the reader has no way of knowing which day that was.
⚠ 'match' is NOT the same thing and must not be pinned as tightly: it recognises what someone
already has, as a substring, longest match winning. Pinning it to an exact tag silently robs
everyone running ':latest' of their note. Hence the family entries below.
'strict_source' is true only when a model refused BOTH kinds of foreign text — another real
language AND an invented one. One model in this file does. One other refuses the invented one
and translates the real one anyway: for that one the option would not do what it promises, so
it is not marked.
⚠ 'the only one HERE', not the only one there is: models measured and left out for being too
slow have managed it too. Refusing is not what turned out to be rare — refusing while still
answering in tenths of a second is.
'load_s' is the wait for the FIRST line: the model read off the disk and put on the card. Paid
once per session, and paid while a game is starting.
⚠ Measured with the card emptied first. Taken one after another the figures triple — the
previous model is still resident — which reads as a warning about the model rather than about
how it was measured.
'languages' is the PUBLISHER'S claim, never our measurement — we have verified none of them.

models.note: What the mod is developed against. 16.1 GB. Followed every instruction, never asked twice. The only one here that refuses both a foreign language and an invented one.

Announces 201 languages and holds 5.3 GB. Followed every instruction without ever being asked twice, and refuses an invented language while translating a real foreign one — so the experimental source rule would not hold for it.
Holds 1.7 GB — less than anything else measured here — and followed every instruction. Four lines in twenty had to be asked again.
Superseded by gemma4:e2b-it-qat: 2.8 GB against 1.7, and one more retry. Followed every instruction, five lines in twenty asked again.
Holds 3.1 GB and followed every instruction, with four lines in twenty asked again.
Holds 7.4 GB, followed every instruction and was never asked twice. It refuses invented words but still translates other real languages, so the experimental source rule would not hold.
Superseded by the 3.5 builds: 5.9 GB against 5.3 for the 9b, and 100 languages announced against 201. Followed every instruction, never asked twice.
Announces the same 201 languages as the 9b and holds 3.1 GB. Followed every instruction without ever being asked twice.
Built for translation and it shows in the prose. Holds 7.8 GB, followed every instruction, and four lines in twenty had to be asked again — its slowest line took 2.8s.
Holds 2.8 GB. The only one here that gave up on a line: it missed one instruction of sixteen, on markers standing next to each other, and left that line in its original language.
One size was run and it has its own line here. If this reads 'latest', the tag moves between versions, so no figure of ours applies to it — check which size it resolves to today.
Several sizes were run and each has its own line here. If this reads 'latest', the tag moves between versions, so no figure of ours applies to it — check which size it resolves to today.
Several builds were run and each has its own line here. If this reads 'latest', the tag moves between versions, so no figure of ours applies to it — check which build it resolves to today.

A whole family rather than one model, so no size or figure is given here. Gemma has no separate system turn — it is merged into the conversation, which makes it more sensitive to how instructions are phrased.

Reasons before answering, so every line costs noticeably more time. Not offered for download either: the smaller build is a 14 GB download and the other 65 GB, both beyond the cards this tool is aimed at.
